scope: Proposition 5.2 (Frozen energy) of the manuscript “Quantitative Near-Kerr Evolution and Generic C2 Future Inextendibility” (preprints/Quantitative-Near-Kerr-Evolution-and-Generic-C2-Future-Inextendibility-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 264 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 cd38cc55e3c203a3), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 44. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix a smooth nearby stationary parameter pair (p, c) and an integer s ≥ 8. The frozen operator Lp,c admits a positive time-local first-jet energy, uniformly for nearby parameters, with full endpoint orders Hs ⊕ Hs−1. On each fixed interior reach its favorable derivative controls ∥Y∥2 Hs−3/2 + ∥BntY∥2 Hs−1 − Cs∥Y∥2 Hs−2(enlarged), Y = (⟨Dy⟩U, DtU), Dt = −i∂t. (5.10) It also controls full mixed physical-nontrapping orders after equation recovery. At the inner and outer differential regions the energy is an ordinary wave current with strict bulk sign and an exiting inner flux. All remaining compact derivative errors have total field order at most s − 1. The compact additions to the differential currents have strictly interior spatial kernel support.
